Contents.Name: body
Contents.Html:
[page[title]]

Let applications define and deliver structured, multilingual content without compiling it into the host.

All platform domainsView the GitHub repositoryRead the documentation

What it owns

  • Pages, page metadata, content, cultures and role visibility.
  • Reusable layouts, components, resources, scripts and templates.
  • Package import and page/app lifecycle event handling.

Why the boundary matters

The site being read now can evolve through governed content APIs while the application host remains stable.

How it fits

The domain is published and tested independently, then composed through cCoder.Core when an application needs the complete platform. That keeps ownership visible while preserving a straightforward application bootstrap.

Getting started

The source, current README, sample hosts and tests live in cCoder.ContentManagement on GitHub. The repository README is the version-specific starting point; the outline below explains how the pieces fit together.

Reference the package

<PackageReference Include="cCoder.ContentManagement" Version="YOUR_VERSION" />

During coordinated local development the repositories may substitute a sibling ProjectReference. Published applications should normally consume the agreed package version so the dependency boundary remains explicit.

Register it in the host

builder.Services.AddContentManagementWeb(/* platform configuration */);
app.StartContentManagementWeb();

Configure and run it

Provide Core data access, app identity, Eventing and the Api/ContentManagement route. A complete page aggregate requires a Page, default-culture PageInfo and default-culture body Content; PageRole records control visibility.

Consume the capability

Use the OData APIs for pages, content, metadata, layouts, components, templates, resources and scripts. Prefer metadata-driven components such as DetailedNav when a page hierarchy can generate its own navigation.

Build and verify from source

git clone https://github.com/ccoder-co-uk/cCoder.ContentManagement.git
cd cCoder.ContentManagement
dotnet build
dotnet test

Use the repository-specific solution and test commands from its README when working on the domain itself; the standalone and acceptance-test hosts show the supported application boundary more accurately than an isolated snippet can.
